title: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn
gist: Netflix released a second trailer for Brad Bird's animated noir/sci-fi film Ray Gunn, which streams on Netflix December 18, 2026, the same day Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 open in theaters. Thin entertainment piece with limited investable content.

themes.theme: Netflix release strategy for Ray Gunn

insights.claim: Netflix will release Brad Bird's animated film Ray Gunn on its streaming service on December 18, 2026, the same day Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 open in theaters, with a limited theatrical screening on December 4, 2026.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Netflix is counter-programming two major theatrical tentpoles with streaming-first family fare, a direct test of streaming vs. box-office holiday demand.
insights.locator: Ray Gunn releases on Netflix on December 18, 2026

insights.claim: Ars Technica frames Netflix's Ray Gunn as alternative holiday family fare for viewers unwilling to face theatrical crowds on the opening day of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Signals Netflix positioning its originals as a substitute for the theatrical outing during peak box-office weeks.
insights.quote: so it will be alternative family fare for those disinclined to brave the holiday theatrical crowds
insights.locator: Ray Gunn releases on Netflix on December 18, 2026

insights.claim: Ray Gunn targets a slightly older demographic with more mature themes than director Brad Bird's Pixar films.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Netflix is funding adult-skewing animation, a segment historically underserved by major studios.

insights.claim: Brad Bird, director of Oscar winners The Incredibles and Ratatouille, developed Ray Gunn over roughly 30 years while its script, co-written with Matthew Robbins, sat in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates how long-shelved legacy-studio projects can migrate to Netflix, which is buying prestige auteur talent.
insights.quote: “stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,”
insights.locator: As previously reported, Bird has directed

insights.claim: Ray Gunn has an all-star voice cast led by Sam Rockwell and Scarlett Johansson, with Tom Waits, Matt Berry, Bobby Cannavale, Alan Tudyk and Patton Oswalt in supporting roles.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Star-heavy casting indicates significant Netflix investment in the title.
insights.locator: In addition to Rockwell and Johansson
